'''House Phoenix''' is the house of '''the future''' — the realm's inventors of what does not yet exist: not better plows but visions of cities, orders, and futures no one asked for. While nine houses turn their gaze back toward the Unification, Phoenix turns its back on the past with intent. It is the only house capable of thinking a truly new thought — and the only one that would sacrifice the entire past for a future it cannot guarantee.

== Philosophy and reputation ==
A Phoenix never asks "how was it done before?" but "why do we do it at all?" The house celebrates the one who fails spectacularly over the one who succeeds modestly, and it keeps '''no chronicle''': it writes plans, not memories.

== Customs ==
* '''The Ash-Will''' — at death, the head of house burns their own life's work, so the heir inherits an empty space, not a burden. The opposite of every other house's inheritance rite.
* '''The annual bonfire''' — the house publicly burns what it considers obsolete.
* '''Burn your own work''' — children are encouraged to burn what they have built and start over. Nothing is sacred, not even one's own.

== The seat ==
[[New-Ash]] stands on the edge of [[the Ash Fields]], on scorched ground where nothing grows — the purest soil, the house says, ready for anything. The castle is torn down and rebuilt every generation, never finished, never the same; a visitor who returns twice never sees the same house. There are no portraits and no graves: the dead burn, their works burn, and a visitor finds nothing to say who was here before.

== Members (396 A.U.) ==
* '''[[Signe Phoenix]]''' (~50), Dawnkeeper and head of house — the realm's boldest visionary, who speaks even of the past in the future tense.
* '''[[Idun Phoenix]]''' (~29), heir — who has begun, quietly, to ask what stood on the ground before.
* '''[[Master Builder Roar]]''' (~44) — lights the yearly bonfire; believes most sincerely of all that to burn is to liberate.
